sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A clumping cactus of the southwestern United States and northern Mexico. Its cylindrical stems are usually 11–23 cm tall and 4.5–10 cm across, sometimes larger.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: The large flowers, about 7–10 cm across, are yellow, sometimes flushed pink to magenta. Purple fruits are described as edible in historical botanical accounts; this is not advice to eat them.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: Only the fruits are documented as food; the sources do not report the stems as food.

sources.title: Flora of North America — Echinocereus dasyacanthus
